explicit_validation.explanation: Both LLM and human evaluations are conducted and evaluate similar aspects (factuality, faithfulness, consistency, relevance), but no direct quantitative comparison, correlation, or agreement analysis between LLM and human judgments is reported.

prompts.notes: Prompts are stated to be adopted from prior work (Saunders et al., 2022) and shown in figures in Appendix G, but the exact full prompts are not fully extracted in the provided text.

guidelines.notes: Annotation guidelines included examples and figure screenshots in Appendix I.

criteria_mapping.notes: LLM evaluates Factuality via Likert scale and pairwise comparison (Factuality Likert Score G, Pair ΔG), while human evaluates document-level Relevance to Aspect, Consistency, and sentence-level Aspect-based Faithfulness (Fully/Partially/Not supported). Factuality is the shared concept, but human evaluates it indirectly via Consistency ratings and Faithfulness proportions without direct score comparison.
